column3: The Hebrew says the LORD “uncovered” Balaam’s eyes; BSB says He “opened” them.
BSB includes an explicit “not” in the conditional clause about turning away; the supplied Hebrew has no separate negative word there.
The Hebrew says “in your eyes” and gives no explicit home destination for returning; BSB says “in your sight” and adds “home.”
The Hebrew names Balak as the speaker, emphasizes sending with a repeated verb, and asks about “honoring” Balaam; BSB uses “he,” “an urgent summons,” and “richly reward.”
The Hebrew emphasizes ability with a repeated verb; BSB gives a single “can” and says “just anything.”
The Hebrew says Balak “sent” to Balaam and the princes, without explicitly naming portions; BSB says he “gave portions.”
The Hebrew says he saw “the edge of the people”; BSB supplies “the camp” in “the outskirts of the camp of the people.”
